company.name: Cobalt Crew Recruitment
company.industry: Staffing and recruitment for warehouse and logistics
company.summary: Cobalt Crew Recruitment is a Manchester staffing agency that places temporary warehouse and logistics workers. Your team of 35 handles recruitment, account management, compliance, shift scheduling, and weekly payroll for client sites across Greater Manchester. You screen hundreds of CVs each week and keep temporary workers compliant and paid on time.
company.customers: Warehouse operators, logistics firms, distribution centres, 3PLs, and manufacturers in and around Manchester that need temporary labour.
tech_signals: Job boards such as Indeed and CV-Library
Excel or Google Sheets for trackers
Payroll software such as Sage or BrightPay

roles.title: Temporary Recruiter
repetitive_tasks: Screen CVs against warehouse and logistics requirements
Post and refresh job ads on job boards
Call and text candidates to confirm availability

roles.title: Payroll Administrator
repetitive_tasks: Calculate hours, overtime, and holiday pay

roles.title: Director or Manager
repetitive_tasks: Review weekly fill rates and margins

strategy.situation: Cobalt Crew Recruitment places temporary warehouse and logistics workers across Greater Manchester. Your 35-person team runs recruitment, compliance, scheduling, and weekly payroll using an ATS, job boards, spreadsheets, and payroll software.
strategy.complication: CV volume, right-to-work expiry checks, and daily shift changes create manual chasing that slows placements and risks compliance misses. Weekly payroll and client reporting add pressure when fill rates are already tight.
strategy.governing_thought: Start with a CV screening agent, a right-to-work expiry agent, and a shift booking agent to cut manual chasing, protect compliance, and fill shifts faster.

key_arguments.headline: Recruiters, compliance staff, and account managers carry most of the repetitive admin
key_arguments.support: Your recruitment team screens hundreds of CVs each week and confirms availability by phone and text. Compliance staff chase right-to-work documents and expiry dates across spreadsheets. Account managers take shift requests, confirm bookings, and handle call-offs while updating CRM and schedules.

key_arguments.headline: These three agents hit high-volume, rule-based tasks with existing tools
key_arguments.support: CV screening, right-to-work expiry checks, and shift booking all follow clear rules and use systems you already have. They create fast proof because the agent can draft, flag, or rank while a human approves. Each one reduces manual chasing in a different department, so the value is visible across the business.

key_arguments.headline: Pilot each agent for two weeks, check outputs, then scale across teams
key_arguments.support: Set narrow rules, keep humans in approval steps, and review errors weekly before expanding. Start with one recruiter pod, one compliance officer, and one account manager as pilot owners. After the pilot proves reliable, rollout scales to the full team and then to more client sites.

maturity.label: Emerging
maturity.note: You have core systems like an ATS, payroll software, and spreadsheets, but most screening, compliance chasing, and shift booking is still manual. No AI agents are in daily use.

roadmap.title: Prove the three phase 1 agents
items: Map CV sources, right-to-work trackers, and shift request channels
Set up CV screening agent with recruiter approval
Set up right-to-work expiry agent with compliance approval
Set up shift booking agent with account manager approval
Review outputs weekly and fix false positives or misses

roadmap.title: Extend into payroll and operations
items: Add timesheet collection and exception agent
Add rota gap and PPE order agent
Train payroll and operations staff on approval steps

roadmap.title: Scale reporting and audits
items: Set monthly KPI reviews for all agents
Expand agents to more client sites and recruiter pods
Document agent rules and owner responsibilities

risks.risk: The CV screening agent rejects good candidates because rules are too rigid.
risks.mitigation: Keep recruiter approval on every shortlist and review false negatives weekly for the first month.

risks.risk: Compliance mistakes create legal or client audit problems.
risks.mitigation: Let the agent flag and draft only. Compliance officers approve all right-to-work and document decisions.

risks.risk: Payroll errors damage worker trust and cause BACS delays.
risks.mitigation: Run the timesheet agent in parallel with manual checks for four weeks and keep human approval before BACS.

risks.risk: Staff resist using new agents or ignore the outputs.
risks.mitigation: Start with volunteer pilot users, show time saved in their own tasks, and give clear owner roles.

risks.risk: Worker or client data is exposed through new tools.
risks.mitigation: Use role-based access, keep data inside existing systems where possible, and review permissions before each rollout.
